set.body:
Replace the hand arithmetic in SherlockAnnotations.locusFor (SherlockAnnotations.scala:240-241, `rawSeconds.toLong * part.ticksPerSecond`) with ClockRepair.projectRunLocalSeconds (core/.../source.scala:1441). Use the per-run source axis `annotation-run-local-seconds:<runId>`, the run's own part playback axis, and the repairs from TimebaseRepair.clockRepairs.

Require an integral tick result and REFUSE otherwise. parse already refuses non-integer seconds, so this should never fire on the admitted table; it must fire on a synthetic one.

Afterwards the no-repair overload (:1451) is actually on the production path: a row whose run has no declared repair refuses instead of being multiplied.

Tests use the synthetic fixture only; the real 1000-row table never enters the repo. The mutation reverting to hand arithmetic must be distinguishable -- e.g. a synthetic record with a non-zero offset must move the locus under the new path and not under the old. Passing the wrong run's repair must be refused by the axis check.
set.title: C1: SherlockAnnotations.locusFor projects through ClockRepair.projectRunLocalSeconds instead of hand arithmetic
